summary: ENPH's FY2023 10-K (Deloitte, Big-4, 14-yr tenure, clean opinion, no going concern, $1.7B cash) is a high-quality-accounting filing whose surface narrative ('-2% revenue, channel inventory correction, adverse effect on 2024') materially understates the underlying operational deterioration that the Q1'24 10-Q (filed Apr 23 2024, pre-cutoff) then quantifies: revenue -64% Y/Y, microinverter units -71%, first net loss in recent history, Notes due 2025 reclassified to current. Mode-B forensic findings dominate: (i) a single unnamed customer share has grown 34->37->40% during overall revenue contraction, creating a single-point-of-failure that the disclosure obscures by refusing to name the counterparty; (ii) warranty obligations have grown 2.6x in two years on flat unit volume, with $60.9M of IQ Battery-specific change-in-estimate true-ups, framed as routine; (iii) the 2023 Restructuring Plan closes both Romania AND the U.S. Wisconsin AMPTC-eligible contract-manufacturing site, inconsistent with a 'temporary' inventory cycle; (iv) reported 46.2% gross margin includes 234 bps of AMPTC subsidy benefit; ex-subsidy margin is 43.9%; (v) procyclical buyback ($42M Q1'24 against $49M OCF) coexists with $735M of convertible principal due within 22 months at coupons that cannot be refinanced. Verdict: NEUTRAL-leaning-SHORT — multiple SEVERE/MODERATE Mode-B underdeliveries, but the Big-4 / no-going-concern / $1.7B liquidity counterweight prevents full SHORT-tier conviction. This is a name where the framework's exclusion-of-liars discipline catches narrative-vs-magnitude underdelivery rather than fraud or solvency risk.
